title: Codebase does not compile on Linux: std.process.Environ{ .block = .global } is Windows-only (7 errors)
resolved_by: src/env.zig portable environment helper, applied to all 96 call sites
scope: Cross-platform build support. No behavioral change on Windows.
symptom: zig build failed on ubuntu-latest with 7 compile errors: std.process.Environ{ .block = .global } only type-checks where Environ.Block resolves to GlobalBlock (Windows, WASI, freestanding). On Linux/macOS, Block resolves to PosixBlock, which has no .global member. The original report named 6 src/ call sites; a full scope pass found 96 total across the repo: 8 in src/ (the report missed src/api/routes/identity.zig) and 88 in tests/ (86 tests/integration/*.zig files plus 2 tests/unit/*.zig files, each with an independently copy-pasted testDbUrl()-style helper).
root_cause_analysis: Environ.Block is a platform-conditional type alias (GlobalBlock on Windows/WASI/freestanding, PosixBlock elsewhere). `.global` is a GlobalBlock-only convenience that reads the PEB directly on Windows; PosixBlock has no equivalent static accessor and must be constructed from libc's `environ` extern instead. The pattern spread to ~90 test files because it was copy-pasted as a small self-contained helper rather than factored into the shared tests/integration/helpers.zig -- which itself independently contained one more copy.
resolution:
Added src/env.zig with globalEnviron(), which branches on builtin.os.tag: returns the original .{ .block = .global } literal on Windows/WASI/freestanding (unchanged behavior), and on POSIX targets builds a PosixBlock from std.c.environ via std.mem.span. Requires linking libc on non-Windows targets, added to every build.zig module that reaches the affected src/ files (idp_config_mod, identity_provider_mod, bpm_main_mod, bpm_src_mod, exe, plus a new env_mod named module for the two files inside the separately-rooted identity_provider_mod, which cannot reach src/env.zig by relative @import since Zig 0.16 forbids escaping a module's root) and to integration_imports plus the two standalone unit-test targets for the tests/ files.

All 8 src/ call sites updated to call env.globalEnviron() directly via relative @import (aliased portable_env in src/config/identity_provider.zig, which already uses `env` pervasively as a parameter name for its own EnvReader test-double abstraction). All 88 tests/ call sites updated mechanically via script: `const portable_env = @import("env");` inserted after the file's `const std = @import("std");` line, and each construction site rewritten to `const <original-name> = portable_env.globalEnviron();`, preserving the original local variable name (`env` in 87 files, `environ` in helpers.zig) so no downstream code needed to change. Three files (adp02_tenant_scope_test.zig, obs03_audit_log_test.zig, obs05_dlq_test.zig) carried a UTF-8 BOM that broke the initial regex's line-start anchor and required a BOM-aware second pass.

Verified: zig build and zig build test both exit 0 natively on Windows (full unit suite, no regressions). zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-gnu and -Dtarget=aarch64-linux-gnu both exit 0 for the main executable. zig build test -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-gnu compiles all 86 test binaries with zero compile errors (run-artifact steps fail only because Windows cannot execute Linux ELF binaries -- expected, not a defect). zig build test-integration against a real local PostgreSQL instance ran to completion with pre-existing, unrelated business-logic test failures (iss0125_cascade_test, iss0602_cross_process_isolation_test) -- confirming the fix compiles and the tests execute, not just that they build.

An earlier verification pass (which produced a first commit and an initial DONE-marked acceptance-criteria list below) checked only zig build test natively on Windows before this scope gap was found by a live CI run on the real ubuntu-latest runner -- src/-only had been fixed, and CI's fresh zig build test failed immediately on the first tests/unit/ file. That CI run also followed one earlier run that hung for 19 minutes with no clear cause before being cancelled; the two are not confirmed related, and the hang was not reproduced on the second (failing, then after this fix passing) attempt.

A second, unrelated Linux-only compile error surfaced once the Environ errors cleared: src/webhook/dispatcher.zig used std.posix.clock_gettime, which does not exist as a free function in this Zig stdlib version (wall-clock access moved to std.Io.Clock.now, requiring an Io handle this call site does not have). Fixed with std.c.clock_gettime, the raw libc extern binding, verified against the same cross-compile targets.

A third issue was found but NOT fixed here, filed separately as it is unrelated to Environ: std.time.nanoTimestamp does not exist for the x86_64-macos target specifically (it compiles for Linux and Windows) in src/admin/tenant_migration.zig and src/api/routes/onboarding.zig. Linux was the platform this issue's acceptance criteria named; macOS was not blocking.
acceptance_criteria: zig build exits 0 on ubuntu-latest -- DONE, confirmed by the real CI runner in this issue's own workflow run
zig build test exits 0 on ubuntu-latest -- DONE after the full-scope tests/ fix; the src/-only fix alone was insufficient and failed on the real runner
No remaining Environ{ .block = .global } in src/ or tests/ -- DONE, 96 of 96 sites fixed; only the platform-gated branch inside src/env.zig itself remains
Environment access goes through a single shared helper -- DONE, src/env.zig globalEnviron()
The build job in .github/workflows/ci.yml drops continue-on-error and becomes a hard gate -- DONE
not_in_scope: std.time.nanoTimestamp missing on x86_64-macos (src/admin/tenant_migration.zig, src/api/routes/onboarding.zig) -- separate stdlib API gap, macOS only, not blocking Linux CI
evidence_file: src/env.zig; build.zig env_mod / link_libc additions; src/webhook/dispatcher.zig currentMicrosecondTimestamp
